Fixes #33

## Summary
- Add a shared uploaded-log filename helper so direct uploaded log files end in `.log.txt`.
- Stage gist uploads through a temporary `.log.txt` file before calling `gh gist create`.
- Stage repository uploads and split chunks with `.log.txt` file names so raw links open as text in browsers.
- Add issue evidence and analysis under `docs/case-studies/issue-33/`, plus a patch changeset.

## Reproduction
Before this change, `/home/user/test.log` generated the user-facing upload name `home-user-test.log`, repository staging preserved `.log`, chunked files had no text extension, and gist uploads passed the original path to `gh gist create`.

The regression coverage in `test/log-text-extension.test.js` verifies the actual gist creation command uses a staged `.log.txt` path, chunks end in `.log.txt`, `.log.txt` is not duplicated, and non-`.log` uploaded log inputs still receive `.log.txt`.

## Verification

- `bun test` (70 pass)

Fixes #31

## Summary
- Route repository-mode uploads to shared `private-logs` / `public-logs` repositories whenever `useSharedRepository` is enabled, regardless of the original file size.
- Keep dedicated per-log repositories available only when callers pass `useSharedRepository: false` or `--no-shared-repository`.
- Update CLI/API docs and config example wording from “large files” to “repository-mode uploads”.
- Add a patch changeset.

## Reproduction
A file under the gist limit uses gist first in auto mode. If `gh gist create` fails, the old fallback path entered repository mode but skipped shared repositories because routing was gated by `fileSize > GITHUB_GIST_FILE_LIMIT`, producing a dedicated `log-*` repository.

## Tests
- Added `uploadLog - gist fallback uses shared repositories for small files by default`, which simulates a small public log, a gist secondary-rate-limit failure, and verifies fallback writes to `public-logs/<repositoryPath>` without creating a dedicated repository.
- Updated dedicated repository collision tests to opt into legacy mode with `useSharedRepository: false`.

## Verification
- `bun run check`
- `bun test`
title: Fix gist fallback shared repository routing

## Summary

Fixes #29 by defaulting large repository-mode uploads to shared `private-logs` / `public-logs` repositories, reusing the old generated repository name as the folder path, and skipping duplicate uploads when that folder already exists.

This PR also keeps the legacy dedicated-repository behavior behind `--no-shared-repository` / `GH_UPLOAD_LOG_SHARED_REPOSITORY=false` / `useSharedRepository: false`, updates `lino-arguments` to `^0.3.0`, and adds the requested issue dossier under `docs/case-studies/issue-29/`.

## How To Reproduce

1. Take a log file larger than 25MB.
2. Before this PR, repository-mode uploads created a dedicated repository derived from the file path.
3. After this PR, the same upload goes into `{user}/private-logs/<generated-folder>` or `{user}/public-logs/<generated-folder>` by default.
4. Re-uploading the same large file path now returns the existing shared-repository entry instead of pushing a duplicate.
5. If you need the old behavior, run `gh-upload-log ... --only-repository --no-shared-repository`.

## Validation

- `bun test test/index.test.js test/cli.test.js`
- `bun test`
- `bun run check`
- Added regression coverage for shared-repository routing, duplicate detection, and the legacy dedicated-repository fallback.
- Added CLI dry-run coverage for default shared repositories and `--no-shared-repository`.

## Summary

Fixes #27 by treating non-zero `gh` / `git` exits as real failures and retrying repository creation with a timestamp-suffixed name when the generated repository name already exists.

During CI verification this also uncovered a Windows-specific repository-upload bug: backslashes in Windows paths were not normalized, which caused repository uploads to copy into missing nested directories. That path normalization is fixed in this PR as well.

## How To Reproduce

1. Upload a log to a private repository for a given file path.
2. Re-run the same file path with `--only-repository --public`.
3. Before this PR, `gh repo create` returned `GraphQL: Name already exists on this account (createRepository)`, but the CLI still printed a successful public upload and pointed at the existing private repository.
4. After this PR, the CLI either fails honestly on command errors or retries with a unique public repository name when the failure is a name collision.

## Validation

- `bun test`
- `bun run check`
- Added library-level regression coverage for repeated `gh repo create` collision failures.
- Added library-level regression coverage for a successful retry after a single collision while preserving `--public`.
- Added Windows path-normalization coverage for backslash-separated file paths.
- GitHub Actions run `24886015374` is green across Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, lint, and changeset checks.

## Case Study And Evidence

- [Issue 27 case study](https://github.com/link-foundation/gh-upload-log/blob/issue-27-05a03800b7e1/docs/case-studies/issue-27/README.md)

## Summary

Fixes #23

- **Detect ENOSPC errors** via `error.code`, `error.message`, and `error.stderr` using new `isENOSPC()` helper
- **Provide actionable guidance** suggesting `~/.claude/debug` cleanup, `/tmp` cleanup, and disk usage commands
- **Prevent wasteful fallbacks**: when gist upload fails with ENOSPC, don't fall back to repository mode (which needs MORE disk space)
- **Suggest `--only-gist`** only when `--only-repository` is forced for a file that fits in a gist (≤25MB) — in auto mode, files ≤25MB already default to gist upload, so this hint is not needed
- **Return structured errors** with `error.code = 'ENOSPC'`, `error.operation`, and `error.originalError` for programmatic handling
- **Add case study** documenting the root cause analysis tracing ENOSPC to the upstream Claude Code infinite debug logging loop ([claude-code#16093](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/16093))

### Key insight

In auto mode, files ≤25MB always use gist upload, which reads the existing file directly and streams it to GitHub's API — no extra disk space needed. Repository mode requires ~2-3x the file size in temp space. The `--only-gist` hint only appears when the user explicitly forces `--only-repository` for a file that fits in a gist.

### ENOSPC scenario matrix

| File size | Mode | Upload path | ENOSPC likely? | CLI output |
|-----------|------|-------------|----------------|------------|
| ≤25MB | auto (default) | gist | Unlikely (no temp space needed) | Disk cleanup suggestions |
| ≤25MB | `--only-gist` | gist | Unlikely | Disk cleanup suggestions |
| ≤25MB | `--only-repository` | repo | **Yes** (needs temp space) | Disk cleanup + `--only-gist` hint |
| >25MB | auto (default) | repo | **Yes** | Disk cleanup suggestions |
| >25MB | `--only-repository` | repo | **Yes** | Disk cleanup suggestions |

### Example CLI output on ENOSPC (default)

```
❌ Error: No space left on device

Suggestions to free disk space:
  • Check ~/.claude/debug for large debug files
  • Clean /tmp directory: rm -rf /tmp/log-*
  • Check disk usage: df -h && du -sh /tmp ~/.claude
```

### Example CLI output when `--only-repository` forced for small file

```
❌ Error: No space left on device

Suggestions to free disk space:
  • Check ~/.claude/debug for large debug files
  • Clean /tmp directory: rm -rf /tmp/log-*
  • Check disk usage: df -h && du -sh /tmp ~/.claude

💡 Hint: This file fits in a gist. Try --only-gist to upload
   without requiring temporary disk space.
```

## Test plan

- [x] 10 unit tests for `isENOSPC()` and `createENOSPCError()`
- [x] 3 new tests validating `--only-gist` hint only appears for forced repo mode
- [x] 3 new tests validating `determineUploadStrategy` always picks gist for ≤25MB files
- [x] CLI ENOSPC detection integration test
- [x] All 54 tests pass (`bun test`)
- [x] Lint passes (`eslint .`)
- [x] Format passes (`prettier --check .`)
- [x] File size check passes

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: feat: handle ENOSPC errors gracefully with actionable error messages

## Summary

Fixes #24

When `gh-upload-log` was called with a file path that did not exist, it printed:

```
⏳ Uploading 0 B (? private)...

❌ Error: File does not exist: /path/to/missing.log
```

The `⏳ Uploading …` line and the blank line before the error were premature and
misleading. The tool now fails immediately with only the error message:

```
❌ Error: File does not exist: /path/to/missing.log
```

## Root Cause

`src/cli.js` only used `fileExists()` to determine the file size (lines 161–163).
It did **not** stop execution there — the upload-status `console.log` at line 175 ran
unconditionally, even for missing files. The `catch` block also emitted an unnecessary
blank line before the error message.

Full analysis: [`docs/case-studies/issue-24/README.md`](docs/case-studies/issue-24/README.md)

## Changes

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `src/cli.js` | Add early `fileExists` guard after the path validation; remove blank line from `catch` block; simplify `fileSize` assignment |
| `test/cli.test.js` | New test: non-existent file produces no `Uploading` line and no leading blank line |
| `docs/case-studies/issue-24/` | Case study with root-cause analysis, timeline, similar-places audit, and proposed solution |

## Test Plan

- [x] All 39 existing tests still pass (`bun test`)
- [x] New test: `CLI with non-existent file does not print upload status before error`
- [x] `bun run check` (lint + format + file-size) passes

## Summary

When uploading a single log file (not split into chunks), the tool now displays a direct link to the raw file content in addition to the repository/gist URL.

- For **gists**: Returns the permanent `raw_url` from the GitHub API (accessible without authentication, even for secret gists)
- For **repositories**: Returns the `download_url` from the GitHub API (includes token for private repos that enables unauthenticated access)
- Displays a warning that the token expires in ~10 minutes for private repositories

### Example output:

```
✅ Gist created (🔒 private)
🔗 https://gist.github.com/user/abc123
📄 https://gist.githubusercontent.com/user/abc123/raw/hash/file.log
```

For private repositories:
```
✅ Repository created (🔒 private)
🔗 https://github.com/user/log-myfile
📄 https://raw.githubusercontent.com/user/log-myfile/main/myfile.log?token=XXX
⚠️  Note: Raw URL token expires in ~10 minutes for private repositories
```

## Changes

- **`src/index.js`**: Modified `uploadAsGist()` and `uploadAsRepo()` to fetch and return raw file URLs via GitHub API
- **`src/cli.js`**: Updated CLI output to display raw URL with appropriate warnings for private repos

body:
## Summary

Fixes #19 - Gist upload fails for ~50MB+ files with HTTP 502, but tool reports success.

### Root Cause Analysis

While GitHub documents a 100MB limit for gist files, the REST API has practical limitations:
- Large POST requests (>25-50MB) cause HTTP 502 errors due to server timeout/payload limits
- The safe threshold matches the **web interface limit of 25MB**

### Changes Made

**1. Fix Success Detection Bug**
- Validate gist URL is present and valid before reporting success
- Throw error with stderr details when gist creation fails

**2. Lower Gist Threshold**
- Changed `GITHUB_GIST_FILE_LIMIT` from 100MB to 25MB
- This matches the web interface limit and avoids HTTP 502 errors

**3. Implement Automatic Fallback**
- When gist upload fails, automatically fall back to repository mode
- Unless `--only-gist` is specified, in which case the error is thrown

**4. Add Self-Test Feature**
- `--test` / `-t`: Run full self-test (1MB, 10MB, 24MB files)
- `--quick` / `-q`: Run quick test (1MB file only)
- Tests actual upload functionality on user's machine

**5. Add Test Utilities**
- `scripts/generate-test-file.mjs`: Generate text files of specific sizes
- Case study documentation in `docs/case-studies/issue-19/`

### Test Results

| File Size | Expected Strategy | Result |
|-----------|------------------|--------|
| 1 KB | gist | ✅ gist |
| 1 MB | gist | ✅ gist |
| 24 MB | gist | ✅ gist |
| 26 MB | repo | ✅ repo |

### Usage Examples

```bash
# Normal upload - files ≤25MB go to gist, >25MB go to repo
gh-upload-log file.log

# Self-test to verify everything works
gh-upload-log --test

# Quick test (1MB only)
gh-upload-log --quick

# Force gist mode (will error if upload fails)
gh-upload-log large-file.log --only-gist

# Force repository mode
gh-upload-log file.log --only-repository
```

### Breaking Changes

- Files between 25-100MB will now use repository mode instead of gist mode
- This is a **fix**, not a breaking change, as these files were failing with HTTP 502 before

---

title: fix: Handle HTTP 502 errors for large gist uploads
